name: RC–B10–0219/2024 – Motion for a resolution
title: JOINT MOTION FOR A RESOLUTION on the 11th year of the occupation of the Autonomous Republic of Crimea and the city of Sevastopol by the Russian Federation and the deteriorating human rights situation in occupied Crimea, notably the cases of Iryna Danylovych, Tofik Abdulhaziiev and Amet Suleymanov
part_text:
The European Parliament is not changing any law here. It is stating its position: it condemns Russia's occupation of Crimea, now in its eleventh year, and the rights abuses there. It asks Russia to free three named prisoners — journalist Iryna Danylovych, activist Tofik Abdulhaziiev and citizen journalist Amet Suleymanov — along with other political prisoners, and to give them medical care. It also asks other countries to keep refusing to recognise the annexation and to tighten sanctions.

- No law changes; Parliament only states its position and makes demands.
- It concerns Russia, Ukraine, and prisoners held in Crimea and Russia.
- Parliament sends the text to EU bodies and to Russia and Ukraine.
